the porous walls destabilize the detonation wave and that the destabilization effect increases with increasing porosity.
the stability is increased by the presence of a slight porosity.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of detonation in the presence of slightly porous walls.
the stability analysis of the detonation wave propagating in the circular pipe with porous wall.
the stability analysis of a planar detonation wave propagating in a circular pipe, with porous walls.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given detonability of a mixture, a porous wall is less stable than an impenetrable one.
the porous wall does not affect the temporal stability of the detonation in the pipe.
, as far as the stability of the fundamental mode is concerned, the porous walls have a stabilizing effect, which is more pronounced the smaller the porosity is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a slight porosity of the walls has a stabilizing effect on the detonation.
the stability is not affected by the porosity of the walls.
a small amount of wall porosity can stabilize detonation in a pipe with respect to transversal perturbations, and the stability threshold is lowered with respect to the non-porous case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of the porosity on the stability of the detonation is very small.

, in the limit of a slightly porous wall, the effect of the porosity on the temporal instability is negligible and thus the impenetrability of the wall can be used to model the effect of the slightly porous wall on the stability of the confined detonation.
a slight porosity in the walls has a stabilizing effect on the detonation, and the degree of stabilization is dependent on the porosity parameter and the wave speed of the detonation.
